title: Hiring manager, senior data and ML, weak answers

questions.text: Tell me about the most impactful model you owned end to end.
How do you decide when a model is ready to ship?
Why this role and why now?
How have you mentored other people?
How do you work with product managers?
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a project.

persona.pushback_style: repeats the question with a narrower ask

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hello Dmitri, thanks for joining. I'm Alma, a data science manager. This is a thirty minute conversation about your experience.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hello Alma, thank you.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How has your week been?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Busy, but good. Thanks for asking.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: I'll ask about a few of your projects and how you work, then leave a few minutes for your questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about the most impactful model you owned end to end.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I built a recommendation model at my last job. We used a standard approach and it improved things for the business. I worked on the data and the training.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was the measured improvement?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I don't remember the exact figure. It was an improvement in the main metric, I believe. The product team tracked it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did you own, and what did the team own?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Mostly the team did the deployment. I helped where I could. I was senior on the project, so I guided people on the approach.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you decide when a model is ready to ship?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: You look at the accuracy and make sure it is good enough. Then you check with the team and ship it. Monitoring after that is also important.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you decide in a specific case?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: On the fraud project we compared the model with the old rules on last month's data. The model caught more cases, so I chose to ship it. I did not look closely at false positives, and that caused complaints later.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How have you mentored other people?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I help junior people when they have questions. I do code reviews and sometimes pair with them. I think a senior person should be available to the team.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about one person you helped grow.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A new analyst joined and did not know experiments. I walked her through one of ours, then let her run the next one while I reviewed. I wanted her to learn by doing.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What tools does the team use?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Mostly Python, a shared feature store and an in-house experiment platform.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is all the time we have. Thanks Dmitri, the recruiter will follow up.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Alma.

notes: Weak for senior: generic, no numbers, unclear own role. The last probe on the project role does not get a concrete answer and the interviewer moves on.
